note: The input bytes are stored in the request buffer; the PROXY v2 signature supplies the CRLFCRLF sequence that allows the short buffer to be finalized as a complete request.
With proxy protocol enabled, the finalized input buffer is handed to the proxy protocol parser before HTTP method parsing.
Because the buffer begins with the binary PROXY v2 signature prefix, execution dispatches to the version 2 parser.
The input-controlled length field is converted into the number of bytes to skip past the PROXY v2 header.
The parser only checks the declared PROXY header size against the C struct size, but it does not require the input buffer length to be at least size bytes before later advancing buffer by size.
The parser advances the buffer pointer by the declared header size, which can move it beyond the actual received input length.
When the declared size exceeds the actual buffer length, this pointer difference is negative and becomes a huge size_t value.
memmem scans from a pointer beyond the real input using the underflowed length, causing an out-of-bounds read.
